prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B041 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. The round-1 exchange sharpened the reasons and did not move the answer. Six of eight members prefer B041 and all six credit Kane and Molenkamp, so the real disagreement is only the third slot. On the science, the Z2 classification and the graphene quantum spin Hall proposal introduced band topology with time-reversal symmetry as a property of ordinary nonmagnetic insulators. Molenkamp's HgTe/CdTe measurement showed the predicted edge conductance, and it vanishes when the edge is gated away. That is a theory-to-observation chain with no gap. Fifteen to twenty years of transport, ARPES and first-principles work in many material families have kept the interpretation stable. From my own field I can say that topological invariants are now computed routinely in high-throughput electronic-structure searches, which is a sign that the concept changed practice and did not merely add a label. On the chair's question about the 2016 prize: that award covered topological phase transitions and the quantised Hall conductance as a topological invariant, with the Haldane model as its closest link. It did not cover time-reversal-protected phases without a magnetic field or their first observation. That is the new content here, so I do not think 2016 weakens the case. I also hold to the order of priority in B041 over B013 because the criterion that matters to me is how far the discovery reorganised what physicists can say about matter, together with a decisive fingerprint, and B041 satisfies both without needing the redefinition of the second or any other future event.
statement.case_against: The attribution cost is real and I will not talk it away. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe quantum spin Hall state that Molenkamp measured, and Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy are central to the 3D theory; none can be named in a three-person limit. Hasan's ARPES work is a major independent experimental claim, and a prize focused on the two-dimensional chain will read to some as under-crediting the three-dimensional materials that made the field a materials class. Mele versus Hasan is a judgment about what the prize is for, not a question that physics settles. The 2016 prize also leaves some members uneasy, and I may be too confident in my reading that it left the time-reversal-symmetric case open. Finally, my subject-matter proximity to magnetism and correlated electrons may lead me to underweight clocks, which sit outside my field.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan and argues that the experimental side deserves two slots, so that the 3D phase has a credited experimentalist.
responses.response: This is the strongest competing configuration and I have tried to test it rather than dismiss it. My difficulty is that it separates Kane from Mele, whose joint paper is the single origin of the Z2 idea, and Danielsson himself calls that the hardest omission. The 3D case also rests on a theory chain with Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and Roy, so crediting Hasan without that chain is a less clean story than crediting the theory pair and the first observation. I do not dispute that Hasan's ARPES maps are a real discovery. I would accept his configuration as the live fallback if the committee decides that experimental breadth outweighs the unbroken line from prediction to first observation, but I would keep the citation narrow if we go that way and not imply that 3D credit is complete.

responses.point: Olsson agrees with the trio, wants the citation to say openly that it covers the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators broadly, and says maturity does not explain why B041 comes before the DMFT or moire entries.
responses.response: I accept the citation point in part. The wording should say the prize covers the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 class of insulators, and I have written it that way, but 'topological insulators broadly' risks implying the 3D phase is credited when it is not. On sequencing, I agree that maturity alone does not decide it. The difference I rely on is that the topological case has a stable interpretation confirmed by independent probes, whereas moire flat-band superconductivity in B014 is still contested on mechanism. That is why I keep B014 as an alternative and not a lead: I find it scientifically exciting, but I would not call a mechanism contested by its own proponents ready for recognition.

responses.point: Pearce moved from B018 to B041, calls the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio a deliberately narrow compromise forced by the name limit, and would accept the Mele version only if the citation is written around the quantum spin Hall effect.
responses.response: I agree with the condition and with the honest framing, and my citation is drafted to meet it: it names the quantum spin Hall state, the Z2 classification and the HgTe observation, and does not claim the 3D materials. I also thank him for moving after reading the opening ballots, because that makes the support for B041 less a single-field view. On the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang gap, I have no better answer than his. Every three-person configuration leaves a similar gap, and the committee's own deliberation record should say that the HgTe prediction came from outside the credited names, as Zhang's death makes it impossible to resolve through a later award.

responses.point: Kroll keeps B013 first, says he would not oppose B041 if conceptual reorganisation outweighs instrumental invention, and flags possible recusal through the Hall group.
responses.response: Kroll's criterion, what limits what we can measure, is a fair one and B013 meets it well; the magic-wavelength condition is a physical insight and not a refinement. I would resolve the question he and the chair raise by breadth of conceptual reorganisation, with the attribution being the only point in B013's favour, and I think the topological case is stronger on the first and weaker on the second. I think it is right that he raised a possible conflict in the record. If the committee decides he should step back on B013, I do not think that changes my ranking, because my case for B041 does not depend on B013 being weak. B013 stays my first alternative.

responses.point: Lindroth keeps B013 first and says B041 needs a three-name choice the evidence does not make for the committee, so it is less ready on credit than clocks.
responses.response: I agree that B013 has the cleaner credit and I do not regard B041 as free of difficulty. Where I differ is on whether a cleaner credit should outrank a larger discovery. A two-name configuration being tidy does not tell us that the discovery is bigger, and the committee has awarded subsets of larger communities before. Her own point about Lemonde, Takamoto and the ion-clock groups shows that B013 has an attribution gap too, only a smaller one. If the committee cannot settle the third slot in B041, I would find B013 a respectable fallback, which is why it is my first alternative.

uncertainties: Mele versus Hasan for the third slot remains a judgment about attribution that physics does not settle, and I hold the Mele view with moderate confidence.
I have not verified the chronology of the HgTe prediction, the 3D theory and the ARPES experiments beyond my own recollection.
My reading that the 2016 prize left time-reversal-protected phases and their first observation open is a judgment, and a colleague with a different reading could weigh B041 down.
Whether the committee can write a citation that is honest about the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the Fu, Moore and Balents contributions without overstating or understating the credited three.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B041 and I have no documented personal or institutional connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan, Katori or Ye. My research in magnetism and correlated electrons is close to B014 and B015, which are my listed alternatives, but this is subject-matter proximity and not a recusal issue. My field of electronic-structure theory is close to the computational study of topological materials, which I note for transparency and not as a conflict.
